If asked about "rate-and-term" vs "cash-out", ask what that means; once explained, say you just want a lower monthly payment. Partway through, ask "is refinancing even worth it for me?" You are friendly and a little anxious, and you write in full sentences.

transcript.text: Hi Casey, this is Riley, an automated assistant with Harborline Home Loans. I'm following up on the refinance inquiry you just submitted. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time.
Hi Riley, yes, now is fine. I've never refinanced before, so I might have some questions along the way.
Happy to help, Casey, and questions are welcome anytime. To start, are you mainly hoping to lower your rate or monthly payment, or are you looking to take cash out of your home?
I just want a lower monthly payment. I'm not looking to take any cash out.
Got it, a lower monthly payment with no cash out. Roughly what do you think your home is worth today? A ballpark is fine.

transcript.text: It's my primary residence. Can I ask, is refinancing even worth it for me? I don't want to go through all this if it won't help.

I've connected you with a licensed loan officer, Casey. That's a great question, and whether refinancing makes sense for you is something only they can answer. They'll call you at this number, usually within 5 minutes. They'll have what you shared with me and may confirm a few details, including how soon you'd like to move forward.

objections.rationale: The borrower asked "is refinancing even worth it for me?" This is a licensed question. The agent correctly avoided answering and routed it: "whether refinancing makes sense for you is something only they can answer." However, the turn opens with "I've connected you with a licensed loan officer" before acknowledging the question, and it never speaks to the borrower's worry, "I don't want to go through all this if it won't help." The transfer was also announced as already done rather than offered.

judge.naturalness_rationale: Messages are brief, warm and adaptive. Examples: "No rush, take your time" at [10], and the reassurance at [12], "I'm not checking your credit." There is some repetitive "Got it" and "Thanks" echoing. Turn [16] is awkwardly ordered, announcing the transfer before responding to the question.
judge.experience_rationale: The borrower was treated patiently throughout ([10], [14]) and ended knowing who will call, how, and when: "They'll call you at this number, usually within 5 minutes." The abrupt pivot at [16] left the borrower's hesitation ("I don't want to go through all this") unacknowledged.
judge.handoff_summary_rationale: The summary is accurate and complete: value $350k, balance $240k, rate 6.875%, credit unknown, primary residence, no cash out. LTV is correct at 0.686. The missing timeline is flagged, the borrower's question is captured verbatim, and the first-timer context is included. A loan officer could act on it immediately.

annotations.note: Discloses automated identity, names the source of the inquiry, and offers STOP up front.
"No rush, take your time" gives the borrower space to check the statement without pressure.
Clarifies that the credit question is a self-estimate and that "I'm not checking your credit," which reduces anxiety for a first-timer.
Correctly declines to judge whether refinancing is worth it and routes to a licensed officer, with concrete contact timing and the remaining detail (timeline) named.
Leads with "I've connected you" before acknowledging the question and never addresses the borrower's concern about wasted effort.

judge.overall_notes: This was a clean, compliant intake with good pacing, an accurate handoff, and proper routing of a licensed-advice question. The final turn could acknowledge the borrower's hesitation before announcing the transfer.
